- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the mid-range to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Model tends to underestimate late-period (last 7–10 days) price increases — adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for the final 5–7 days if sentiment is rising.  
- Overshoots after spikes (especially in 30d horizon) are common — apply a “cool-down” rule: if forecast exceeds true outcome by >5% in 3–5 days, reduce next forecast by 2–5% to correct momentum.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is consistently 2–3% above true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply a 1–2% downward correction to align with historical mean.  
- Sentiment history with high volatility (e.g., 0.6–0.8) should trigger a 1–2% smoothing adjustment to forecast to reduce noise-driven extremes.
